notes.33.0: Iael (33) is a divine name. In 37 κατήλειψεν means 'anointed', but it may stand for κατέλειψεν 'left [him]', which would match God's order to leave Adam there. In 39 ὅπως ᾖ καθήμενος ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ is third person ('so that he may be sitting above him'); the sense seems to be that Adam will sit above the devil, and it is rendered so.
notes.26.0: ἕως ἂν πλανήσῃς, literally 'until you lead astray', is taken as 'so as to lead astray'. In the clause on the limbs, ὧν may also mean 'of all those whom you lured', i.e. none of the limbs the deceived humans have.

nodes.text: Then Eve says to them: Listen, all my children and my children's children, and I will tell you how our enemy deceived us. It happened, while we were guarding paradise, that we each guarded the part allotted to him by God; and I guarded in my lot the south and the west. And the devil went into Adam's lot, where the male animals were; for God divided the animals between us, and all the males he had given to your father, and all the females he gave to me, and each of us kept watch over his own.

And the devil spoke to the serpent, saying: Get up, come to me, and I will tell you a word by which you may profit. Then the serpent came to him, and the devil says to him: I hear that you are wiser than all the animals, and I have come to observe you; and I have found you greater than all the animals, and they keep company with you; yet you bow down to the lesser one. Why do you eat of the weeds of Adam and his wife, and not of the fruit of paradise? Get up and come, and let us have him thrown out of paradise through his wife, just as we too were thrown out through him. The serpent says to him: I am afraid that the Lord may be angry with me. The devil says to him: Do not be afraid; only become my vessel, and I will speak through your mouth a word by which you will be able to deceive him.

And at once he hung himself over the walls of paradise, about the hour when the angels of God went up to worship. Then Satan took the form of an angel and sang hymns to God as the angels did; and leaning out from the wall I saw him, like an angel. And he says to me: Are you Eve? And I said to him: I am. And he says to me: What are you doing in paradise? And I said to him: God placed us [here] to guard [it] and to eat from it. The devil answered me through the mouth of the serpent: You do well, but you do not eat from every plant. And I say to him: Yes, we eat from every plant except one alone, which is in the middle of paradise, concerning which God commanded us not to eat from it, since [otherwise] you will certainly die.

Then the serpent says to me: As God lives, I am grieved for you, because you are like cattle. For I do not want you to be ignorant of this; but get up, come, listen to me and eat, and perceive the worth of the tree. And I said to him: I am afraid that God may be angry with me, as he told us. And he says to me: Do not be afraid; for as soon as you eat, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like gods in knowing what is good and what is evil. But God, knowing this, that you will be like him, begrudged you and said: You shall not eat from it. But you, look closely at the plant, and you will see great glory about it. And I looked closely at the plant, and I saw great glory about it. And I said to him that it was lovely to the eyes to look upon, and I was afraid to take of the fruit. And he says to me: Come, I will give [it] to you; follow me.

And I opened to him, and he came inside into paradise, and went through ahead of me. And after walking a little he turned and says to me: I have changed my mind, and I will not give you [it] to eat. He said this wishing to entice me and destroy me utterly. And he says to me: Swear to me that you will give [it] to your husband too. And I said to him: I do not know with what oath I should swear to you; but what I know I tell you: By the throne of the Master and the cherubim and the tree of life, I will give [it] to my husband too to eat. And when he had received the oath from me, then he came and climbed up on it; and on the fruit, which he gave me to eat, he put the poison of his wickedness, that is, of his desire; for desire is the head of every sin. And I bent the branch down to the ground and took of the fruit and ate.

After saying these things to me, he spoke to the serpent in great anger, saying to him: Since you have done this and have become an ungrateful vessel, so as to lead astray those who are slack of heart, cursed are you beyond all the cattle. You will be deprived of the food that you used to eat, and you will eat dust all the days of your life; on your breast and belly you will go, and you will be deprived both of your hands and of your feet; there will not be left to you ear or wing or a single limb of all those with which you lured [them] in your wickedness and caused them to be thrown out of paradise; and I will put enmity between you and his offspring; he will watch for your head, and you for his heel, until the day of judgment.

And Eve rose and put her hand over her face, and the angel says to her: Lift yourself up from earthly things. And Eve gazed into heaven, and saw a chariot of light coming, [drawn] by four shining eagles, whose glory it was not possible for anyone born from a womb to tell, nor to see their face, and angels going before the chariot. When they came to the place where your father Adam lay, the chariot stopped, and the seraphim [were] between the father and the chariot. And I saw golden censers and three bowls, and look, all the angels with frankincense and the censers and the bowls came to the altar and blew on them, and the smoke of the incense covered the firmaments. And the angels fell down and worshipped God, crying out and saying: Holy Iael, forgive, for he is your image and the work of your holy hands.

And again I, Eve, saw two great and fearful mysteries standing before God. And I wept from fear, and I cried out to my son Seth, saying: Get up, Seth, from the body of your father Adam and come to me, so that you may see what no one's eye has ever seen; and they are praying for your father Adam.

Then Seth rose and came to his mother, and says to her: What is the matter with you? And why are you weeping? She says to him: Look up with your eyes and see the seven firmaments opened, and see with your eyes how the body of your father lies on its face, and all the holy angels with him, praying for him and saying: Forgive him, Father of all, for he is your image. So then, my child Seth, what will this be? And when will he be handed over into the hands of the invisible Father, our God? And who are the two Ethiopians standing by at your father's prayer?

Seth says to his mother: These are the sun and the moon, and they too are falling down and praying for my father Adam. Eve says to him: And where is their light, and why have they become black? And Seth says to her: They cannot shine before the Light of all things, and for this reason the light has been hidden from them.

While Seth was speaking to his mother, the angels, lying on their faces, sounded trumpets and cried out with a fearful voice, saying: Blessed is the glory of the Lord over his works; he has had mercy on the creature formed by his hands, Adam. When the angels had cried these things aloud, one of the six-winged seraphim came and snatched Adam away to the Acherusian lake and washed him in the presence of God. And he lay there three hours; and so the Master of all, sitting on his holy throne, stretched out his hands and lifted Adam up and handed him over to the archangel Michael, saying to him: Take him up into paradise, to the third heaven, and leave [him] there until that great and fearful day which I am about to bring about in the world. And Michael the archangel took Adam and led him away and anointed him, as God had told him, at the pardoning of Adam.

So after all these things the archangel made request about the burial of the remains; and God ordered that all the angels should come together before him, each according to his rank. And all the angels were gathered, some holding censers and others trumpets; and the Lord of hosts mounted [his chariot], and the winds drew him, and cherubim set over the winds and the angels of heaven went before him; and coming to where the body of Adam was, they took it. And they came into paradise, and all the plants of paradise were stirred, so that all those born from Adam grew drowsy from the fragrance, except Seth, because he had been born according to God's decree.

So the body of Adam lay on the ground in paradise, and Seth grieved greatly over him. And the Lord God says: Adam, why did you do this? If you had kept my commandment, those who are bringing you down into this place would not be rejoicing. Yet I tell you that I will turn their joy into grief, and your grief I will turn into joy; and I will turn [you] back and seat you in your [former] dominion, on the throne of the one who deceived you; and he will be cast into this place, so that [you] may be sitting above him. Then he and those who listened to him will be condemned, and they will grieve much and weep when they see you sitting on his honoured throne.
